info.name: TriloPlan Backend API
info.description:
Backend API for the video-chat platform (User app, Host app, Admin app). See BACKEND_PLAN.md, BRD.md and DEVELOPMENT_ROADMAP.md in the repo for full context.

## Status (as of this export)
Built and live: Phase 0 (foundations), Phase 1 (auth + profiles), Phase 3 (host discovery + presence), a wallet/ledger core (built alongside Phase 4 since billing needs a wallet to exist), Phase 4 (calls: signaling + per-minute billing), Phase 5 (1:1 chat), Phase 6 (gifting), Phase 7 (live broadcasting), Phase 8 (withdrawals — request/slab-conversion/status lifecycle is real; only the actual gateway payout call is still dev-stubbed, see Known limitations), Phase 9 (admin panel: KYC/withdrawal approval queues, pricing/gift config, sub-admin RBAC, audit log, account suspension, moderation report queue, analytics dashboard), Phase 10 (18+ toggle with per-broadcast content gating by age verification, and screen-capture event logging with threshold-based escalation to the moderation queue), Phase 11 (hardening: device-fingerprint multi-accounting and call-collusion fraud signals — both auto-file into the same moderation queue rather than auto-suspending; a call reaper that recovers any call left ringing/ongoing by a server restart or a dead billing timer; wallet ledger reconciliation, on-demand and hourly; per-user rate limiting on call-initiation, gift-sending, and moderation endpoints; plus a follow-up pass closing gaps found during end-to-end testing: per-host commission overrides (BR-COM-03), push-notification fallback wired for incoming call / gift received / low balance / withdrawal status change, a host-follow feature so 'a followed host going live' (BR-NOTIF-01) has something to notify, and CI now actually runs the full suite against a real Postgres + MinIO instead of failing to boot).
Not yet built: real payment gateway recharge.

## Auth flow — TWO separate identities, on purpose
Calls inherently involve two parties (a user and a host), so this collection keeps **two independent logged-in identities** side by side rather than one shared "current session":
- `userAccessToken` / `userRefreshToken` / `userId` — set by **Auth — Login → 2. Verify OTP — User App**.
- `hostAccessToken` / `hostRefreshToken` / `hostId` — set by **Auth — Login → 4. Verify OTP — Host App**.

Every authenticated request below has an explicit `Authorization: Bearer {{userAccessToken}}` or `{{hostAccessToken}}` header — whichever the endpoint actually requires — so there's no ambiguity about which identity is being used, and no dependency on request order beyond "run Auth — Login first."

Phone numbers must be E.164 format (`+<countrycode><number>`, e.g. `+919876543210`) — required now that OTP delivery can go through real Twilio SMS. In non-production environments (this one, right now), OTP request responses still include `devCode` regardless of whether Twilio is configured — auto-saved to a collection variable by a test script — so you don't have to check a real phone to keep testing. Access tokens expire after 15 minutes; use **Auth — Session → Refresh Access Token** (pick the right token pair) to get a new one.

## Recommended run order (Collection Runner-safe, top to bottom)
Health → Auth — Login → Profile (Me) → Admin — Identity & KYC → Hosts — Discovery & Presence → Wallet → Calls → Chat → Gifts → Live Broadcasting → Withdrawals → Admin → Moderation → Auth — Session. Admin — Identity & KYC runs early (right after Profile) specifically because Withdrawals needs the host's KYC already approved, and that approval requires an admin login. This ordering matters: Calls needs the host online + rate set (Hosts/Profile folders) and the user's wallet funded (Wallet folder) before it can succeed, Gifts and Live Broadcasting's gift step also need the wallet funded, Withdrawals needs the host's KYC approved and payout details on file (Profile (Me) → steps 5-9) plus the beans those gift sends earned the host, and Auth — Session is last since Logout clears a token pair.

## Known limitations right now
- OTP delivery uses real Twilio SMS when the backend has Twilio credentials configured; otherwise (or always, in tests) it falls back to dev-mode logging, still returning `devCode` in the response either way for easy testing.
- Wallet recharge has no real payment gateway yet — `POST /wallet/dev-credit` is a dev-only stand-in (hard-blocked in production) that lets you fund a test user's wallet directly.
- Video/audio tokens are real Agora RTC tokens (via the `agora-token` SDK) — nothing stubbed there anymore. Actually joining a channel with one still needs a real Agora client SDK (web/mobile), which is outside what Postman/curl can demonstrate.
- KYC documents go to a real private S3 bucket via presigned upload/download URLs (Profile folder, steps 1-4) — nothing stubbed there anymore.
- Presence and call-billing scheduling are in-memory on a single server instance for now (will move to Redis/a job queue once provisioned) — functionally identical for testing purposes.
- Presence toggles, call lifecycle events, chat messages, gift events, and live-broadcast events also broadcast over Socket.io (`presence:update`, `call:incoming`, `call:accepted`, `call:ended`, `call:low-balance-warning`, `chat:message`, `gift:received`, `gift:requested`, `live:chat`) to connected clients. Postman can't demonstrate that (it's not a plain HTTP call) — connect with `auth: { token: "<accessToken>" }` and listen for the relevant event from an actual client to see it live.
- Live chat messages (`POST /live/broadcasts/:id/chat`) are NOT persisted anywhere — they only fan out over Socket.io to whoever is currently in the broadcast's room at that instant (`BACKEND_PLAN.md` §4). There's no history endpoint; a viewer who joins late has missed everything said before they joined.
- Chat/gift push notifications (for an offline recipient) are dev-mode logging only — no FCM configured yet. The underlying action (message sent, gift request raised) still succeeds regardless; push is best-effort on top.
- Screenshot/recording prevention is a client-side control (Android `FLAG_SECURE`, iOS capture-change detection) the backend cannot enforce — only configure (`secureMode` on call/live-join responses) and log (`POST /moderation/capture-event`, BR-MOD-03). See BACKEND_PLAN.md §5.
- The gift catalog has real admin CRUD now (Admin folder, `POST/PATCH /admin/gifts`) — Rose/Heart/Crown are just the `npm run db:seed` starting point, not the ceiling.
- Withdrawals: beans debit, slab conversion, minimum/frequency checks, and status lifecycle are all real (`POST /withdrawals`), and the admin approval queue above the auto-approve threshold is now real too (Admin folder → '9. Decide Withdrawal'). The actual bank/UPI transfer still isn't — Razorpay payout credentials aren't verified (same reason recharge isn't built), so `dev-resolve-payout` stands in for the gateway's webhook. It's dev-only and hard-blocked in production. Withdrawal policy (min ₹5, auto-approve under ₹1000, 1 request per 7 days) and slabs (1 paise/bean under 50,000 beans, 2 paise/bean at 50,000+) are `npm run db:seed` placeholders, same as commission/beans-rate.

request.description: Confirms the API is up and can reach the database. No auth required.

item.name: Auth — Login
item.description: Shared by the User app and the Host app — both apps hit the same endpoints, differing only in the `role` sent on first-ever verify for a phone number. Admin login (email/password) is a separate flow, not yet built (Phase 9). Run this folder top to bottom — it logs in BOTH a user identity and a host identity, kept as separate variable sets (see collection description).

request.description:
Sends a 6-digit OTP to `phone` (must be E.164, e.g. `+919876543210`). Rate-limited to 5 requests per 15 minutes per IP — you'll get a 429 if you spam this.

Sends a real SMS via Twilio if the backend has Twilio credentials configured; falls back to server-side-logged dev mode otherwise. Either way, the response includes `devCode` (the actual code) in non-production environments — never rely on `devCode` being present in production.

response.name: Validation error

request.description:
Verifies the OTP and logs in — creating a new USER account on first-ever verify for this phone number. `role` is only honored on brand-new signups; an existing account always keeps its original role, so this can't be used to escalate a user into a host or vice versa.

Saves `userAccessToken` / `userRefreshToken` / `userId`.

response.name: OK — new or existing user
No active OTP / expired / already used

request.description: Same endpoint as step 1, for the separate HOST test phone number.

Same endpoint as step 2, with `role: "host"` and the separate host phone/code. Creates the user row, an empty host_profiles row, AND a host_wallets row in one step, on first-ever verify for `hostPhone`.

Saves `hostAccessToken` / `hostRefreshToken` / `hostId` — kept separate from the user identity's variables.

response.name: OK — new or existing host

item.name: Profile (Me)
item.description: Shared by both apps. `Update Host Profile` is HOST-only (uses `{{hostAccessToken}}`, 403 for a USER account). Other requests default to `{{userAccessToken}}` but work identically for either identity.

request.description: Returns the logged-in user's profile. If the account role is HOST, the response also includes a `hostProfile` object; USER accounts get `hostProfile: undefined` (omitted).
All fields optional — send only what you want to change. `dob` must be `YYYY-MM-DD`. Note: setting `dob` here does NOT set `ageVerified` — that only happens via KYC review (not yet built).

HOST accounts only — a USER account calling this gets a 403. All fields optional.

`ratePerMinutePaise` is in the smallest currency unit (paise), same convention as the wallet, to avoid floating-point issues. Example: 6000 = ₹60.00/minute — set to this value so the Calls folder's examples line up (₹60/min → 1000 paise per 10s billing tick).

request.description:
KYC documents live in a private S3 bucket (no public access) — this generates a short-lived (5 min) presigned PUT URL for a new object key scoped to your account. `contentType` must be one of: `image/jpeg`, `image/png`, `application/pdf`.

Saves `kycUploadUrl` and `kycDocumentKey` for the next two steps.

body.raw: This is placeholder file content for testing the upload flow.

request.description:
Goes straight to S3, not to our backend — the presigned URL from step 1 carries its own auth (a signature in the query string), so no Authorization header here. Swap the body for an actual file in a real client (multipart isn't needed; this is a raw PUT of the file bytes).

In Postman itself, if you want to upload a real file instead of this placeholder text: change the request Body type to "binary" and select a file — just make sure its content type matches what you requested in step 1.

body.raw: This is placeholder file content for testing the upload flow.

request.description:
Records that the document at `key` (from step 1, now actually uploaded via step 2) was submitted as part of a new KYC attempt, and moves `kycStatus` to `pending`. Up to 4 documents (id_front/id_back/selfie/address_proof, each type once) can be submitted together in one attempt — this example submits just one to keep the demo flow simple. An admin reviews and approves/rejects it via the Admin — Identity & KYC folder.

Every document's `key` must start with `kyc/<your own user id>/` — submitting a key that isn't yours gets a 403, since nothing else stops one account from claiming a document it never actually uploaded.

response.name: Forbidden — key doesn't belong to you

request.description: Returns the current KYC status plus the latest attempt's documents, each with a fresh 5-minute presigned GET URL to view it (we never store a permanent view URL — it would go stale, so a new one is generated on every call).

Same flow as steps 1-4 above, but for the HOST identity — a withdrawal request (Withdrawals folder) requires the host's own KYC to be approved (BR-EARN-03), not the user's. Saves hostKycUploadUrl and hostKycDocumentKey.

body.raw: This is placeholder file content for testing the upload flow.

request.description: Goes straight to S3, same as step 2 above — no Authorization header, the presigned URL carries its own auth.

body.raw: This is placeholder file content for testing the upload flow.

request.description: Moves the host's kycStatus to pending — approved via the Admin — Identity & KYC folder's '7. Decide KYC — Approve Host (Admin)' request (Phase 9's real admin KYC review queue), which runs right after this folder, not a self-service step in this folder.

Structured gallery items (media type + optional video duration) — separate from `PATCH /me/host-profile`'s bulk `gallery` URL array (still works, untouched) so the admin app can view/moderate/delete one item at a time (see Admin folder's gallery endpoints). Saves `galleryItemId`.
Every gallery item this host has added, newest first.
Scoped to items this host actually owns — a 404 either means the id doesn't exist or belongs to someone else, same as every other 'delete my own X' endpoint here.

HOST accounts only. Either `{ "type": "upi", "vpa": "..." }` or `{ "type": "bank", "accountHolderName": "...", "accountNumber": "...", "ifsc": "..." }`. Required before a withdrawal can be requested (BR-ACC-03) — snapshotted onto each withdrawal request at creation time, so changing it later doesn't retroactively alter a request already in flight.

item.name: Admin — Identity & KYC
item.description:
Admin/sub-admin login plus the KYC approval queue (BR-ADM-05) — split out from the Admin folder and run early, right after Profile (Me), because Withdrawals' first request needs the host's KYC already approved, and that approval now requires a real admin login (Phase 9) rather than the old self-service `/me/kyc/dev-approve`.

Requires an ADMIN account to already exist — there is no signup flow for role=admin/sub_admin by design (auth.routes.ts only ever creates USER/HOST rows). Run `npm run db:seed-admin -- {{adminPhone}} {{adminEmail}} {{adminPassword}}` against the target environment once before running this folder.

Steps 1-2 log in via phone+OTP (still supported, handy for local/dev scripting); step 2b logs in the same account via email+password instead — the admin web app's actual design (Phase 9 follow-up). Either sets `adminAccessToken`/`adminId`; the rest of this folder and the Admin folder don't care which one ran last.

request.description: Requires an admin account to already exist for this phone number — run `npm run db:seed-admin -- {{adminPhone}}` against the target environment once before running this folder (admin accounts have no signup flow by design, see db/seedAdmin.ts).
`role` is omitted — an existing account (created by db:seed-admin) keeps its role regardless of what's sent here (auth.routes.ts), it's only honored for brand-new signups.

item.name: 2b. Admin Login — Email + Password (Design's Primary Method)

request.description: The admin web app's actual login screen — email + password, not phone/OTP (steps 1-2 above stay as a dev/scripting convenience, both work against the same seeded account). Deliberately returns the same generic 401 for 'no such email' and 'wrong password' so this can't be used to enumerate admin emails.

response.name: Unauthorized — wrong password (same error as unknown email)

request.description: ADMIN only (BR-ADM-03) — a sub-admin cannot create another sub-admin, even one scoped to every permission. In a real rollout you'd usually grant a narrower set (e.g. just `finance`); this example grants all three so the same sub-admin identity below can exercise every gated endpoint.
moderation permission. Should include the host from Auth — Login once Profile (Me) has submitted their KYC document.
moderation permission. The 'SUBMITTED DOCUMENTS' detail screen — attempt number, submitted-at, and every document on the submission with a fresh 5-minute presigned view URL each.

response.name: Not found — no pending submission for this user

request.description: moderation permission. Replaces the old dev-only `/me/kyc/dev-approve` self-approval escape hatch — this is the real Phase 9 approval queue. Also verifies age (`ageVerified: true`) if the host's `dob` is on file (BR-ACC-04) — the KYC document is the actual basis for that, not a self-declared checkbox.

item.name: Hosts — Discovery & Presence
item.description: Primarily consumed by the User app (browse/discover) and the Host app (presence toggle). `Toggle My Presence` is HOST-only — run it before the Calls folder so the host is actually callable.

query.description: true | false. Omit to show all active hosts regardless of presence.
One of: rate_asc, rate_desc, online_first. Omit for unsorted.

request.description: Browse hosts available for calls/chat. Excludes suspended/banned host accounts automatically. Any authenticated account (user or host) can call this.

HOST accounts only. Sets the host's online/offline status, which immediately affects what shows up in `List Hosts` with `onlineOnly=true` — and whether `POST /calls` will accept a call to this host at all.

Also broadcasts a `presence:update` Socket.io event — `{ hostId, isOnline }` — to every connected socket client. To see this live: connect a Socket.io client to `{{baseUrl}}` with `auth: { token: "<accessToken>" }` in the handshake and listen for `presence:update`. Postman's plain HTTP requests can't demonstrate the socket side of this — that part needs to be tested from an actual client (or a small script).
Phase 11 implementation follow-up, BR-NOTIF-01 'a followed/favorite host going live'. USER only. Idempotent — following twice is a no-op, not an error.
Idempotent — unfollowing something never followed is also a no-op, not an error.

item.name: Wallet
item.description: No real payment gateway yet (BACKEND_PLAN.md §2/§3, pending a business decision) — `Dev-Credit My Wallet` is the stand-in that lets you fund a test USER wallet directly so the Calls folder has something to bill against. Hard-blocked in production.

request.description: Returns `{ balancePaise }` for a USER account or `{ beanBalance }` for a HOST account — shape depends on the token's role. Swap the Authorization header to `{{hostAccessToken}}` to see the host variant.

Credits the USER identity's wallet directly — the escape hatch for testing call billing without a real payment gateway. USER-role tokens only (a host gets 403); disabled entirely when `NODE_ENV=production`.

`amountPaise` example: 10000 = ₹100.00, enough for several 1000-paise (₹10) billing ticks at the ₹60/min rate set in the Profile folder's example.

item.name: Calls
item.description:
Per-minute-billed video/audio calls between a USER (caller) and a HOST (callee) — BACKEND_PLAN.md §1/§4. Run in order: Initiate → Accept (or Reject) → [wait, or poll Get Call] → End.

Billing is server-authoritative: once accepted, a real background job bills a fixed-size tick (currently 10 seconds' worth) off the USER's wallet and credits the HOST's bean balance every ~10 seconds while the call is `ongoing` — you don't have to do anything to make that happen, just leave the call open and poll `Get Call` or `Get My Wallet` to watch the totals move. The commission % and beans conversion rate are snapshotted onto the call at creation time, so admin config changes never retroactively alter an in-flight or completed call.

Prerequisites for `Initiate Call` to succeed: the host must be online (Hosts folder) with a rate set (Profile folder), and the user's wallet must hold at least one minute's worth of the host's rate (Wallet folder).

request.description:
USER accounts only. Gates on: host exists/active/online, host has a rate set, neither party already has an active call, and the caller's wallet balance covers at least one minute at the host's rate. Creates the call in `ringing` status and pushes a `call:incoming` socket event to the host.

Saves `callId` for the rest of this folder.

Either participant can fetch the current state — poll this while a call is `ongoing` to watch `tickCount`/`totalAmountPaise`/`totalBeans` climb roughly every 10 seconds as the real billing scheduler runs.
Only the target host of a `ringing` call can accept it. Moves status to `ongoing`, starts the real 10-second billing scheduler for this call, and pushes a `call:accepted` socket event to the user.

Alternative to Accept — only valid while the call is still `ringing`. No money ever moves for a rejected call. Not part of the main happy-path run below (Accept already consumed this call); use it on a freshly-initiated call if you want to see the rejection flow.

Either participant can end an active (`ringing` or `ongoing`) call — swap the Authorization header to `{{hostAccessToken}}` to end it as the host instead. Stops the billing scheduler and returns the final totals. Calling this on an already-ended call returns 409, not a silent success.

item.name: Chat
item.description: Free 1:1 messaging between a user and a host (BACKEND_PLAN.md §4 — self-built, not a vendor product). Delivered live over Socket.io to a connected recipient (`chat:message` event) and falls back to a push-notification stub otherwise (no FCM configured yet — logs server-side instead of actually pushing).

request.description: USER or HOST — sends `content` to `recipientId` (a user can only message a host and vice versa; 400 otherwise). Creates the conversation on first message between a given user/host pair, reuses it after. Saves `chatConversationId` for the rest of this folder.

response.name: Created
response.body:
{
  "conversationId": "3f1c9e2a-1234-4a1a-9c8e-2f1b7e2a9d10",
  "messageId": "7a2b8c1d-5678-4a1a-9c8e-2f1b7e2a9d10",
  "senderId": "8e946734-1b08-4956-b4e1-bb96ddea0135",
  "content": "Hi! Are you available for a call?",
  "createdAt": "2026-08-13T10:00:00.000Z"
}

request.description: Same endpoint, sent as the host back to the user — reuses the same conversation created in step 1 rather than creating a second one for the same pair.
Every conversation the caller is part of (as either the user or host side), newest activity first, with the other participant's basic info.
Newest-first message history for one conversation. Either participant can read it — anyone else gets a 403, not a 404 (so you can tell "not yours" apart from "doesn't exist").

response.name: OK

item.name: Gifts
item.description: Priced in real currency, same debit/commission/credit mechanism as call billing (both go through wallet.service.ts's transferUserToHost) — BACKEND_PLAN.md §1. Only a USER can send a gift; only a HOST can request one.

request.description: Active gifts only, cheapest first. Seeded by `npm run db:seed` (Rose ₹10, Heart ₹50, Crown ₹200) — no admin catalog CRUD yet (Phase 9). Saves `giftId` (the cheapest one) for step 2.

response.name: OK

request.description:
USER only. Debits `giftId`'s price from the sender's wallet, applies the current commission %, credits the host's beans — identical math to a call-billing tick. `context`/`contextId` are optional (a gift doesn't have to be tied to a specific call/chat instance) — `{{giftId}}` comes from step 1, `{{chatConversationId}}` from the Chat folder (run that first, or just delete this field).

Broadcasts `gift:received` to the recipient over Socket.io.

HOST only. Moves no money — just a live prompt (`gift:requested` over Socket.io, or a push-notification stub if the user has no live connection) for the user's client to open the gift picker. `suggestedGiftId` is optional.

item.name: Live Broadcasting
item.description: One host, many viewers, over the same Agora project used for calls — the host gets a PUBLISHER token, viewers get SUBSCRIBER (read-only). Live chat and in-broadcast gifts fan out to everyone currently watching over a Socket.io room; live chat is NOT persisted (BACKEND_PLAN.md §4) — there's no history endpoint to call.

request.description: Phase 10, BR-MOD-01. Any authenticated role can check this — lets a host's app decide whether to even offer the 'mark as 18+' toggle before trying to start a broadcast with it. Off by default (`npm run db:seed`); toggled via Admin → '23. Toggle Adult Mode Config (Admin)'.
HOST only, and only one live broadcast at a time per host (409 if you're already live). Saves `liveBroadcastId` for the rest of this folder.

response.name: Conflict — already live

request.description: Currently-live broadcasts only, each with the host's basic info and a live `viewerCount` (concurrent, not peak). This is the User app's discovery screen.

USER only. Idempotent — joining twice without leaving doesn't inflate the viewer count. Updates `peakViewerCount` if this makes a new high. In a real client, this is also the moment to connect a Socket.io client (if not already connected) so live chat/gift events actually arrive — Postman can't demonstrate that half.

Either the broadcasting host or a currently-joined viewer (403 otherwise — join first). Fans out `live:chat` to everyone in the broadcast room over Socket.io; nothing is persisted, so there's no history to fetch back.

response.name: Forbidden — haven't joined

request.description: The exact same endpoint as the Gifts folder's Send Gift — gifting-in-live reuses that pipeline unchanged (BACKEND_PLAN.md §4). The only difference `context: "live"` makes: the resulting `gift:received` event is ALSO fanned out to the whole broadcast room, not just sent privately to the host, so every viewer sees it.
Idempotent — leaving twice, or leaving without ever joining, is a no-op success either way.

request.description: Exchanges a refresh token for a new access/refresh pair. The presented refresh token is invalidated immediately, even on success — it's single-use (rotation), so calling this twice with the same token will 401 the second time by design.
